title: Muthoot Microfin Ltd - 544055 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Muthoot Microfin Q1 FY27: record Q1 disbursement of INR2,644 crore, cost of funds down to 10.13%, credit cost 2.6%, and AUM growth guidance raised to 20%.
summary.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as the start of an execution-led turnaround, with disbursements of INR2,644 crore (about 49% above Q1 FY26) and collection efficiency near 98%. Cost of funds fell 14 bps QoQ to 10.13% before the benefit of the AA- CRISIL upgrade, and credit cost eased to 2.6% from 2.8%. PPOP rose about 43% YoY and 3% QoQ, and AUM grew 18% YoY. Management raised FY27 AUM growth guidance to 20%, ROA to the upper end of 3.3%, and ROE to around 18%, and said NIM expansion would show from Q2.

financial_highlights.change: about 49% above Q1 FY26; highest Q1 ever

financial_highlights.value: Up about 43% YoY and about 3% QoQ
Flat QoQ; management cited about 50 bps YoY expansion in Q1
financial_highlights.change: Full-year FY27 NIM guided 12.3%-12.5%; management said 12.5% upper end is achievable

segments.name: Joint Liability Group (JLG)
segments.commentary: Yield on group loans about 24.85% after a rate hike from 23.5% at end of Q1. Remains one of three priority products.

segments.name: Individual loans
segments.commentary: About INR3,200 crore book with 0.02% 30+ delinquency and no 60+ or 90+. Yield about 23.5%. Built on a creamy layer of about 8.5-9 lakh customers with 700+ scores. Repayments are 100% digital.

segments.name: Gold loans (referral and co-lending)
segments.commentary: Disbursing about INR100 crore per month since April; about INR350-360 crore disbursed to date. Q1 was almost entirely referral business. Co-lending split is 60% on Muthoot Microfin's book and 40% on the parent's book. Referral earns 1.5%.

segments.name: Loan against property and consumer durables
segments.commentary: LAP yield 18%-22%. Consumer durable loans are a pilot of about INR500 crore at 22%-23% yield, funded through CP at about 8.1%-8.2%.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guidance raised to 20% for FY27.
Disbursement plan exceeds INR12,000 crore for FY27, averaging about INR1,000 crore per month.
Cost of funds targeted to reach single digits by end of FY27, with AA- rating benefit still to flow through.
FY27 ROA guided at 3.3% (upper end expected), ROE around 18% (upper end). Management expects 4%-4.5% ROA within about 18 months and about 5% by FY30.
Credit cost guidance of 2.7%-3.5% for FY27, now expected to be better; long-term normalised range 2%-2.25%.
NIM guidance 12.3%-12.5%; NIM expansion expected from Q2 as liquidity drag eases.
Digital collection to reach about 75% by 2030, possibly earlier. Currently about 40%, improving about 6% per quarter.
Branch count to reach 1,740-1,750 by end FY27 from about 1,670 now.
capex_capacity: Branches about 1,670 now, targeted at 1,740-1,750 by end FY27. Expansion focus on Andhra Pradesh and Assam, plus north, east and west geographies.
AUM per branch rose to INR8.65 crore from about INR7 crore a year ago. Management targets INR12-13 crore per branch.
Gold loans use parent Muthoot Finance branches for storage and assessment, so no separate gold branch capex is needed.
Consumer durables pilot of INR500 crore to be expanded depending on results.
demand_pricing: Industry AUM contracted, but quality is improving. Management says larger, well-capitalised players are gaining share. Industry active customers have fallen from about 8 crore at peak to about 6 crore.
Muthoot's active customers fell 0.6% QoQ and declined YoY. Management attributes this to write-offs and closures and says new customer acquisition should lift the base from Q2.
Group yield raised to 24.85% from 23.5% at end of Q1, with no further hike planned for now. Management said the benefit should go to NIM rather than customers.

Liquidity is ample. About INR5,000 crore of sanctions are in hand, plus INR1,000 crore under CGFMU of which only INR200 crore has been drawn. About 20% of AUM is targeted for CGFMU cover; the application is pending.
Management said El Nino rainfall deficit fell from 43% to about 12%. Less than 2% of customers are directly exposed to agri activity in sensitive regions.

qa_highlights.question: Can disbursement return to INR1,000 crore per month, and can AUM growth exceed 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR1,000 crore per month is achievable, with FY27 disbursement above INR12,000 crore. Q1 at INR2,644 crore was the slowest quarter, and Q2 onward should rise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the blended yield, given that the incremental cost of borrowing fell while NIM stayed flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended portfolio yield is about 23%. Reported yield is diluted by non-performing assets in the denominator. Management said Q1 NIM is up about 50 bps YoY, and yield expansion will follow as collections from NPAs improve.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Assam flood or the broader monsoon risk affect the book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company has no exposure to upper Assam, where floods are seasonal, and its lower-Assam portfolio is unaffected so far. Natural calamity insurance covers all customers, including drought.

qa_highlights.question: How do the direct assignment (DA) income and gold referral and co-lending work?
qa_highlights.answer: DA income is booked under net gain on fair value changes, not interest income. Q1 DA was about INR355 crore, and FY26 DA was about INR1,600 crore. Gold co-lending began only at quarter-end, so about 98% of Q1 gold business was referral.

qa_highlights.question: What is the credit cost guidance for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance of 2.7%-3.5% has been beaten, with Q1 at 2.6%. Management expects FY27 to come in below 2.7%, with a long-term normal of 2%-2.25%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for margins and ROA/ROE?
qa_highlights.answer: NIM guidance is 12.3%-12.5%, with the upper end expected. FY27 ROA is guided at 3.3% (upper end) and ROE at about 18%. Management targets 4%-4.5% ROA in about 18 months and about 5% by FY30.

qa_highlights.question: What are the MFI vs non-MFI mix targets?
qa_highlights.answer: AUM mix is at 76:24 (JLG to non-JLG) now and is expected to end FY27 at about 70:30. Management's long-term target is 55:45 on AUM and 60:40 on balance sheet after DA.

risks_watch: Cost of funds must reach single digits by end FY27; benefit of the AA- CRISIL upgrade and CGFMU drawdown (only INR200 crore drawn of INR1,000 crore; about 20% of AUM targeted cover, application pending) are not yet in the Q1 numbers.
NIM expansion is guided from Q2, but Q1 NIM was flat QoQ with negative carry from excess liquidity; watch whether disbursement recovery consumes liquidity and lifts NIM toward 12.3%-12.5%.
Disbursement must average about INR1,000 crore per month (FY27 plan above INR12,000 crore) versus INR2,644 crore in Q1; AUM growth guidance of 20% depends on this ramp.
Active customers fell 0.6% QoQ and declined YoY; management expects base growth from Q2 but this depends on new acquisition in new geographies (Andhra Pradesh, Assam, north, east, west).

Credit cost of 2.6% is below the 2.7%-3.5% guidance; sustainability versus the long-term 2%-2.25% normal and exposure to El Nino and Assam floods are open questions, though management cites insurance cover and less than 2% agri exposure in sensitive regions.
Gold co-lending and referral and the consumer durable pilot (INR500 crore at 22%-23% yield) are early-stage; Q1 gold business was about 98% referral and co-lending only began at quarter end.
key_quotes: this is a turnaround that we have been talking about the quarter 1 performance actually reflects what strategy that we have developed and articulated, it is getting into motion and getting into execution.
In the quarter, we have reduced our cost of fund from 10.27% to 10.13%, 14 basis point reduction has already happened in the Q1 itself.
We feel that in the financial year, we should be able to come into single digits in terms of our cost of fund and availability of fund is already there.
So we are likely to overachieve that in terms of credit cost. We are looking at 2.7% at the lower spectrum, but we'll be better than that for sure, the way the asset quality is panning out.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat throughout, with management describing Q1 as the start of an execution-led turnaround and raising FY27 AUM, ROA and ROE guidance. Answers were more cautious on the specifics of blended yield, the DA income split and the CGFMU timing, and on the active customer decline, where management acknowledged a minor QoQ and YoY drop.

adds.what: Branches from about 1,670 to 1,740-1,750 by end FY27 (Andhra Pradesh, Assam, north, east, west expansion)

growth.why: Management raised FY27 AUM growth guidance to 20% (from prior), backed by disbursement plan above INR12,000 crore (about INR1,000 crore/month), ~INR5,000 crore sanctions in hand and branch expansion to 1,740-1,750 by end FY27; Q1 disbursement INR2,644 crore (+49% YoY) and PPOP up ~43% YoY support it, though branch-count and pricing levers are only partially detailed.
